audit.summary: False used Proposition3.14, a used source/sink mismatch, and a specified-class Lefschetz counterexample are demonstrated. A local folded-word mismatch is Minor. Main coordinate-ring falsity is not established; sufficient factorial and orientation repairs are verified within stated scope.
limitations: P1 — Proposition 3.14 does not follow from coordinate-ring containment — Counterevidence: Counterexample is not asserted to satisfy all of Theorem3.13's stronger deletion/contraction data. No main braid-theorem counterexample.

P2 — The leading induction vertex is a source under the printed graph convention — Counterevidence: Reversing graph convention gives correct neighbor set; exchange algebra is unchanged. Main theorem not refuted.

P3 — The specified Lefschetz class vanishes on an admissible two-dimensional torus — Counterevidence: Laurent coordinate ring and mixed Tate cohomology hold. Corrected-center Poincare symmetry is not refuted. Other form dlogt1 wedge dlogt2 works on this torus.

P3 — The specified Lefschetz class vanishes on an admissible two-dimensional torus — Counterevidence: The all-frozen Laurent coordinate ring and mixed Tate cohomology survive. A nonzero dlog t1 wedge dlog t2 repairs this particular torus only; no universal replacement class theorem is certified.

P4 — A G2 folded mutation word is not the projection of its listed lift — Counterevidence: Both orbit words palindromic, so reversing composition cannot resolve it. Listed lift passes independent braid comparison; no long-braid theorem refutation.

proposition.claim:
The working group in [1, PDF p. 2] is complex, simple and simply connected, with a fixed pinning and opposite Borel subgroups. A double word \(\beta=i_1\cdots i_m\) has letters in \(\pm I\) and Demazure product \(w_0\). Weighted flags are points of \(G/U_+\); strict relative position must be distinguished from relative position allowing a torus factor. The quotient \(\mathring R_\beta\) is asserted smooth, affine, factorial and irreducible, of complex dimension \[D=d(\beta)=m-\ell(w_0).\] The rightmost positive distinguished subexpression runs backwards from \(u_m=w_0\). Its solid positions form \(J_\beta\), with \(|J_\beta|=D\). The Deodhar torus has character variables \(x_e\), determined by their orders on the boundary divisors. A solid index is mutable when the corresponding almost-positive subexpression has initial value \(\mathrm{id}\). Frozen boundary divisors lie outside the open braid variety, and the frozen variables are units there.

Theorem 1.1 identifies \(\mathbb C[\mathring R_\beta]\) with the cluster algebra of the constructed seed. This statement is distinct from the general criterion in Proposition 3.14 and from the particular cohomological conclusion in Theorem 6.8. A seed on an affine variety, as defined on PDF p. 18, requires its initial torus to be an open dense subset. It does not already require every mutated variable to be regular on that variety.

Proposition 3.14 [1, PDF pp. 21–22; printed pp. 1099–1100] states that if \(X\) is affine, factorial and irreducible, \(\Sigma\) is an integral sink-recurrent seed on \(X\), and \(\mathbb C[X]\subset U(\Sigma)\), then \(\mathbb C[X]=A(\Sigma)\). The proof first treats the cluster tori as embedded in \(X\), and then invokes a codimension-two complement. The stated containment does not supply those embeddings.

Equation reference: eq:rankone. Set \[X=\mathbb A^1\times\mathbb G_m,\qquad R=\mathbb C[x,y,y^{-1}],
 \qquad T=(\mathbb G_m)^2\subset X.\] Take \(x\) mutable, \(y\) frozen, \(d=(1,1)\), and exchange column \(\widetilde B=(0,1)^t\). A full skew matrix is \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), with \(\omega=-\operatorname{dlog}x\wedge\operatorname{dlog}y\). Mutation gives \[
 xt=1+y,\qquad t=x'=(1+y)/x .\] The ring \(R\) is a localization of a polynomial unique factorization domain, so every geometric hypothesis on \(X\) holds. The seed is integral. Its mutable graph has one vertex and no arrows, hence it is sink-recurrent. Its exchange rows even span \(\mathbb Z\), so it is really full rank. The special frozen-row condition in the standing Assumption 3.11 also holds: the frozen row is \(+1\) and there is no other mutable column. Thus neither that standing assumption nor full rank eliminates the example.

There are only two alternating rank-one clusters, since mutation returns \(x\). Consequently \[U(\Sigma)=
 \mathbb C[x^{\pm1},y^{\pm1}]\cap\mathbb C[t^{\pm1},y^{\pm1}]
 \quad\hbox{inside }\mathbb C(x,y).\] Every generator of \(R\) belongs to both Laurent rings: in the second one, \(x=(1+y)/t\). Therefore \(R\subset U(\Sigma)\), exactly as required.

Nevertheless, \(t\) is a cluster generator and is not regular on \(X\). At the admissible point \((x,y)=(0,1)\), a regular extension of [eq:rankone] (#eq:rankone) would imply \(0=2\). Equivalently, \(\operatorname{ord}_{\{x=0\}}t=-1\). Hence \(R\ne A(\Sigma)\). This is a counterexample to the proposition, with all its hypotheses verified, rather than merely an unfilled proof step.

The induced mutated-torus morphism is \[\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C[t^{\pm1},y^{\pm1}]\longrightarrow X,\qquad
 (t,y)\longmapsto((1+y)/t,y).\] It sends every \((t,-1)\), \(t\ne0\), to \((0,-1)\). It is therefore not an open immersion. Together with the initial torus it still misses \(\{x=0,\ y\ne-1\}\), a codimension-one set. Exact reviewer-written arithmetic independently checked two distinct preimages and the nonzero numerator at \((0,1)\); the ring argument above establishes the general discrepancy. See the saved `aux_induction/exact_counterexample_checks.json`.

repair.content:
Add full rank, factoriality, regularity of all initial and one-step variables, frozen units and R subset U. Proof uses units/irreducibility/primality and principal-open tori covering codimension one. Adequate for actual factorial braid application with explicit preceding regularity argument and consistent orientation; normal-only generality unresolved.

Reverse graph convention globally or consistently use source/outgoing recurrence and criterion; local exchange x2x2'=x1+x3 shows x3 is unit on divisor and must be frozen.

Use full-dimension exponent D/2-p and target D-p+s when D even, but also require appropriate nondegenerate class or alter prescribed form. Only torus-specific alternative verified; no general replacement theorem asserted.

Replace folded word in this row by(3,6,3).
